slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 10, treat 10.1.1 Searching for Keys as an algorithmic claim. To search, compare the key with the current node. Equality succeeds, a smaller key moves left, and a larger key moves right. Reaching a null child proves absence under the invariant. The work is O(h), where h is tree height. Calling it O(log n) without a balancing assumption is incorrect. A chain of n nodes has linear height, while a well-balanced shape has logarithmic height. Keep the structural parameter h visible until the implementation actually enforces a height bound. The ordering rule applies to every descendant, not only immediate children. At a node with key ten, every key in its left subtree must be less than ten, including a right descendant several levels below the left child. Checking only parent-child comparisons can accept a tree that is locally plausible and globally wrong. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.

slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 10, treat 10.2.1 Removing Nodes with Zero or One Child as an algorithmic claim. A leaf can be replaced with an empty link. A node with one child can be replaced by that child’s subtree because all its keys already satisfy the ancestor bounds. The code moves the old node into a local unique owner, then moves its surviving child into the original owning link. This ordering is more robust than reaching through an object while assigning over the unique pointer that owns it without carefully sequencing access. After the child is detached, destroying the old node no longer destroys the surviving subtree. Root deletion uses the same operation as child deletion because both are owning links. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.title: Failure clinic — A local ordering check missed an ancestor violation
keyPoints: A validator accepts a left child smaller than its parent, but a deeper right descendant is larger than the root.
Local comparisons are insufficient.
Carry ancestor bounds through recursion so every node is checked against its full permitted interval.
A tree can satisfy every immediate comparison used by a weak validator and still misdirect search.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 10, treat Failure clinic — A local ordering check missed an ancestor violation as an algorithmic claim. A validator accepts a left child smaller than its parent, but a deeper right descendant is larger than the root. Local comparisons are insufficient. Carry ancestor bounds through recursion so every node is checked against its full permitted interval. A tree can satisfy every immediate comparison used by a weak validator and still misdirect search. Deleting a two-child node removes several unrelated keys. Inspect the successor removal and ownership transfers. A raw successor pointer is only an observer; clearing its parent’s owner before extracting a retained child can destroy too much. Compare the entire sorted snapshot with the reference set after the failing operation. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.
